page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-2xCPU-16GB is a Cloud Native family virtual server running on the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an AMD EPYC 7542 processor. The configuration includes 2 vCPUs allocated on a shared basis, operating at a clock speed of 2.0 GHz. It is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per core. No local storage or GPU hardware is bundled with this instance, though it includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Performance benchmarks indicate that this server is positioned for lighter workloads. The shared AMD EPYC CPU scores in the bottom 10% for both single-core and multi-core stress-ng tests. Memory bandwidth is mixed, with read-only large block performance at a weak 33.08 GB/sec, while write large block performance reaches an average 26.54 GB/sec. Cryptographic and compression tasks show moderate capability, with gzip single-threaded compression achieving an average 25.46 GB/sec, whereas multi-threaded bzip3 decompression falls into the bottom 10% at 19.14 GB/sec. Database and web serving capabilities are limited, as demonstrated by a weak PassMark database score of 1338.69 and a poor static web serving throughput of 2.34 GB/sec.

Given its shared CPU allocation and modest processing benchmarks, this server offers a highly cost-efficient profile for memory-intensive but compute-light applications. The 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio provides a generous memory allocation without the cost of dedicated compute cores. It is best suited for workloads such as lightweight caching, small-scale database operations, basic text processing, or development environments that require a larger memory footprint but do not demand sustained, high-performance CPU throughput.
